title: PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) completes Rp 6.54 trillion shareholder loan from PT Jasamarga Transjawa Tol (JTT) to PT Jasamarga Jalanlayang Cikampek (JJC)
text: The article reports that PT Jasa Marga Tbk (JSMR) facilitated a shareholder loan (SHL) of Rp 6.54 trillion between its subsidiaries PT Jasamarga Transjawa Tol (JTT) and PT Jasamarga Jalanlayang Cikampek (JJC) on 17 September 2026. JSMR holds 65% of JTT and JTT holds 40% of JJC, and the loan is intended to bridge JJC’s refinancing and other operational needs with an interest rate within the market range. The transaction reduces JSMR’s cash and cash equivalents by roughly Rp 6.54 trillion and increases other receivables by the same amount, while its total liabilities were about Rp 100 trillion as of June 2026; the loan has no immediate impact on revenue or expenses, and JSMR’s first‑half 2026 toll revenue rose 6.8% to Rp 9.5 trillion, net profit about Rp 1.9 trillion and EBITDA grew about 8%. Panin Sekuritas analyst Elandry Pratama recommends a “buy on weakness” for JSMR with a target price of Rp 3,800–4,000 per share, noting the loan supports JJC’s liquidity while increasing intra‑group funding exposure.

title: Ahead of Haji Isam’s entry into PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN), director Alastair Gordon Christopher McLeod sells shares worth Rp2.47 billion
text: Director Alastair Gordon Christopher McLeod of PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) sold 185,200 shares at Rp13,352 each, totaling about Rp2.47 billion, reducing his holding to 3,8148 million shares (0.01% voting rights). The sale was reported to OJK on 22 Sep 2026, and BYAN’s share price fell 9.71% (1,275 points) to Rp11,850 on that day, though the stock remains up 16.18% week‑to‑date and 7.73% over three months with a market cap of roughly Rp400 trillion. Meanwhile, PT Jhonlin Baratama, a subsidiary of the Jhonlin Group owned by Haji Isam, signed a conditional share purchase agreement to acquire 10,000,000,500 BYAN shares (about 30% of the total 33.33 billion) pending conditions, following prior agreements by major shareholders Low Tuck Kwong and Elaine Low who together hold 62.25% of BYAN.

title: PT Victoria Investama Tbk (VICO) approves cash dividend of Rp8 per share for FY 2025
text: PT Victoria Investama Tbk (VICO) approved at its extraordinary general meeting on 18 September 2026 a cash dividend for the 2025 financial year of Rp8 per share, totaling Rp121,736,605,264. The dividend will be payable to shareholders of record on 30 September 2026, with payment scheduled for 22 October 2026, following cum-dividend and ex-dividend dates set between 28 September and 1 October 2026.

title: Analyst highlights nickel stock recommendations and sector outlook amid RKAB and HPM regulatory pressure
text: David Kurniawan of PT Indo Premier Sekuritas says nickel issuers remain under pressure in 2026 because of global oversupply, uncertainty over RKAB approval and new HPM regulations. Year‑to‑date, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) fell 9.57%, PT Trimegah Bangun Persada Tbk (NCKL) dropped 18.67%, PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) slid 11.3%, PT Central Omega Resources Tbk (DKFT) declined 8.97%, PT PAM Mineral Tbk (NICL) plunged 64.61%, while PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) posted a modest 0.63% gain. The analyst notes that integrated issuers such as ANTM and INCO have stronger resilience due to diversified portfolios and healthy capital structures. He expects the sector’s outlook to improve gradually in 2027 if RKAB approvals proceed smoothly and cost‑efficiency measures take effect.

title: PT Fast Food Indonesia Tbk (FAST) to Hold Extraordinary General Meeting on 14 October 2026 to Approve Board Changes and Articles Amendment
text: PT Fast Food Indonesia Tbk (FAST) will hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting (RUPSLB) on 14 October 2026. The agenda seeks shareholder approval for changes to the board of directors and an amendment to the articles of association, specifically Article 3 on the company's purpose, objectives and business activities, to align with the 2025 Indonesian Standard Industrial Classification (KBLI). The meeting will be conducted in a hybrid format via eASY.KSEI and physically at the Gelael building, with voting rights limited to shareholders recorded in the KSEI list as of 21 September 2026 who hold written confirmation or a proxy. FAST reported a net loss attributable to its parent entities of Rp56.74 billion for the first half of 2026, a sharp decline from the Rp138.75 billion loss in the same period of the prior year.

title: PT Guna Timur Raya Tbk (TRUK) shares jump 9.94% as Gabriel Rey and Andry Hakim acquire 20% stake
text: PT Guna Timur Raya Tbk (TRUK) shares surged 9.94% to close at Rp1,715 on Tuesday (22 Sep 2026), after rising 45.34% in the week and 114.38% in the month, following Gabriel Rey (through PT Pukul Rata Kanan) and Andry Hakim (through PT Hakimson Growth Capital) buying a combined 20% stake from PT Catur Dharma Anugerah Surya. PT Pukul Rata Kanan purchased 65.25 million shares at Rp428 each (≈Rp27.93 billion) and PT Hakimson Growth Capital bought 21.75 million shares at the same price (≈Rp9.31 billion), for a total transaction value of about Rp37.24 billion. The price rise gives the investors potential capital gains of roughly Rp83.98 billion for Gabriel Rey and Rp27.99 billion for Andry Hakim, totaling nearly Rp112 billion, and the stock touched the Auto Reject Top (ARA) level. In the first half of 2026, TRUK reported revenue of Rp19.24 billion, down from Rp19.62 billion a year earlier, and a net loss of Rp3.76 billion, widening from Rp3.13 billion in H1 2025.

title: PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) announces interim dividend payment schedule for FY 2026
text: PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) disclosed that it will distribute a cash interim dividend for the 2026 fiscal year. The dividend totals US$10 million, equivalent to approximately Rp 1.42 per share, and was approved by the Board of Directors and the Board of Commissioners on 18 September 2026. Key dates are: cum‑dividend on the regular and negotiation markets on 30 September 2026, ex‑dividend on 1 October 2026; for the cash market, cum‑dividend on 2 October 2026, ex‑dividend on 5 October 2026, with the recording date set for 2 October 2026 at 16:00 and payment scheduled for 22 October 2026. For the six‑month period ending 30 June 2026, the company reported net profit attributable to its parent of US$17.29 million, retained earnings of US$98.90 million and total equity of US$1.11 billion, while its shares closed at Rp 620, down 2.36 % on 22 September 2026.

title: Profit Grows for Multiple Regional Development Banks Despite Credit Contraction
text: Profit rose across a number of regional development banks (BPDs) in August 2026 despite declines in credit portfolios, with PT Bank Pembangunan Daerah Jawa Barat dan Banten Tbk (BJBR) posting a 58.7% YoY increase in net profit to Rp923.26 billion while its credit fell 3.7% YoY. Similar patterns were observed at Bank BPD DIY, Bank Jatim (BJTM), Bank Banten (BEKS), Bank Sumsel Babel, Bank Jakarta and Bank Nagari, where net profit growth ranged from about 2% to 284% and fee‑based income rose, offsetting modest credit contractions or, in the case of Bank Banten, strong credit expansion.

title: PT Siloam International Hospitals Tbk (SILO) Secures Rp14.5 Trillion Syndicated Loan to Finance Acquisition of 14 Hospitals
text: On 22 September 2026, PT Siloam International Hospitals Tbk (SILO) secured a syndicated loan facility of Rp14.5 trillion to fund its acquisition of 14 hospital operators from First Real Estate Investment Trust. The loan is provided by a consortium of banks—BNI, Bank CIMB Niaga, BCA, Bank DBS Indonesia, MUFG Bank and HSBC—and shareholders have pledged guarantees on the acquired hospital assets. The transaction is valued at approximately Rp6.91 trillion, split into a first tranche of Rp4.08 trillion for eight targets and a second tranche of Rp2.83 trillion for six targets, representing about 67.57 % of Siloam’s equity of Rp10.23 trillion as of 31 March 2026. The directly impacted targets are PT Sriwijaya Mega Abadi (SMA), PT Eka Dasa Parinama (EDP), PT Sentra Dinamika Perkasa (SDP), PT Graha Indah Pratama (GIP), PT Dasa Graha Jaya (DGJ), PT Nusa Bahana Niaga (NBN) Divisi Rumah Sakit, PT Buton Bangun Cipta (BBC) Divisi Rumah Sakit, PT Menara Abadi Megah (MAM) Divisi Rumah Sakit, PT Prima Labuan Bajo (PLB), PT Perisai Dunia Sejahtera (PDS), PT Bayutama Sukses (BS), PT Primatama Cemerlang (PC), PT Graha Pilar Sejahtera (GPS) and PT Yogya Central Terpadu (YCT) Divisi Rumah Sakit, which will become subsidiaries of Siloam.

title: Stock Moves of Salim to Prajogo Conglomerate Issuers: Who Delivered the Highest Returns?
text: The article reviews the year‑to‑date (YTD) share‑price performance of issuers affiliated with Salim Group, Astra Group and Prajogo Pangestu group in 2026. Salim affiliates PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk (LSIP) surged 36.82% to Rp1,635, reporting 16% revenue growth to Rp2.69 trillion and a 25% net‑profit rise to Rp891 billion, while PT Salim Ivomas Pratama Tbk (SIMP) and PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF) posted gains of 7.89% to Rp615 and 3.32% to Rp7,000 respectively. Astra affiliates PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO) climbed 25.28% to Rp3,370 with revenue up 13.2% to Rp10.9 trillion and net profit up 22.6% to about Rp1.15 trillion, PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) rose 13.22% to Rp8,350, and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) fell 16.27% to Rp24,700. Prajogo Pangestu affiliates PT Petrosea Tbk (PTRO) dropped 50.57% to Rp5,400 despite a 59.56% revenue jump to US$543.98 million, and PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) also slumped sharply, underscoring weaker YTD returns for the Prajogo group.
